Our grandmothers would shake their heads, the mothers would roll their eyes, and the daughters would push them away with a stern look. It was all a joke.

But I was done with it. I was tired of them watching every single move that I made.

Then I heard the news. All the secret societies of the world. Of the world.

Illuminati, Masons, Knights Templar, Shriners, Skull and Bones.

All of them.

The one place I thought would be safe. The one place the "them" couldn't get a hold of me. That place, the only place that I thought I was free.

It was shattered.

I knew I had to do something.

So I found them.

I couldn't even remember their names. Just the faces. All the faces. All the women's faces. The ones I knew all my life. The ones I passed in the halls. The ones I ate with in the cafeteria. The ones I sat beside in the classes. The ones I knew... knew... knew.

I just couldn't figure out how it all made sense.

It took a while to figure it out. But once I did... I saw the world in a new light.

The world I was watching. I was sure of it.

It had been so long... the days before, the months before, the years...

But I could feel them still. They were always there. Watching, waiting, whispering their words in my dreams.

They couldn't speak in the real world. That was when they were the quiet ones. The ones that I had never noticed. Until this morning.

When the men said something to each other... and then started to speak to each other in a low voice... and I knew.

John opened his eyes. He was lying on a mat. The cold floor sent a chill down his spine. John sat up. His head spun.

The lights were dark.

They all were. John thought back. He could recall some details of the last few days - or maybe weeks? At this moment, it didn't really matter. All that he knew was that he was here.

Where was here?

The last thing John knew was the clock tower of the university. He always went to see his watchmakers.

What a pity. His watch no longer showed the time. He was certain it would have failed long ago. His watch was his most prized possession.

His watch was gold with a moon dial. The day dial was a disc that had the days of the month in place of the numbers. It was made to tell the story of John's life.

John could no longer remember his life.

How could he know that if his watch had stopped working when he was old? It had stopped ticking decades ago.

He could not remember his life.

How could that be? It seemed like only yesterday he was there.

He stood up, brushing the dust off. John had just realized how dark it was.

There was no way he could make it through this night, no chance. John looked around. There wasn't any help in sight. No sign of anyone alive. A man lay on the floor beside him. John bent over him. It was a man. The man was slumped over and motionless.

He was dead.

John could not help but think this was a nightmare. John sat down and laid his head down in his lap.

His heart hurt.

He wanted to go back. How did he get here? The memory seemed so clear yet so vague.

How did he get here? He thought.

John was going to give up. He had no hope. He couldn't even manage to sit up straight.

"Very well," he said, his voice hoarse with exhaustion, "It appears the test was... rather effective. Regardless, the exam is over, so you may make your way out of the classroom."

It was an old paper, however, one that had been used by a hundred of his classes, and now had all its original content erased with nothing but the ink stains showing.

As a few more students made their way out, DeSouza sat back, closing his eyes for a moment. He had always had a love for this subject, and found it very rewarding to see his students improve and begin to pick up the subtleties of the topic, however it was always a bit of a pain to retest his classes, this time being no different. He opened it and saw it was a test. The students had not filled out the exam, instead had written on it their answers. The student sitting in front of him hadn't gotten the answer correct.
